text:
Maya: Heads up — we started seeing a spike of 502s from hosted-inference in eu-north around 10:20 UTC. Multiple customer escalations landing in CS. Any ops available?
Sahil: I'm on it, pulling gateway and edge metrics now. 502 gateway rate up ~7x vs baseline, p50 latency to backends also higher.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-783 created (severity: high) — paging oncall.
Leah: Noticed retransmit and PMTU errors on the egress interface to provider ASN 64512. Lots of ICMP unreachable and DF-set packets getting dropped. Could be MTU/fragmentation blackhole.
Juan: Can confirm from a few test traces — mtr shows packet loss at provider hop and TCP handshake stalls. Traceroute shows MTU path-change: MSS reduced to ~1200 on some hops.
Maya: CS reports some customers saw auth failures and billing API errors alongside the 502s. Likely timeouts causing token refresh flakiness for some flows. Full example from customer logs: "502 gateway upstream reset".
Sahil: Grabbing tcpdump from edge -> provider to validate. Quick grep shows lots of TCP retransmits + ICMP "frag needed" messages.
Sahil: Snippet from edge capture:
```
10:23:14.123 IP client->edge: SYN
10:23:14.150 IP edge->provider: [DF] seg=1400 -> ICMP frag-needed from provider-hop
10:23:14.151 TCP retransmit
...
```
Leah: Looks like provider is blocking ICMP fragmentation-needed or dropping fragments. Classic PMTUD blackhole.
Juan: Short-term mitigation idea: apply TCP MSS clamping on our eu-north egress so don't send large frames that require fragmentation. Also consider routing failover for affected prefixes to eu-west for high-tier customers.
Oncall-Tim: I'm going to implement MSS clamp (1400) on the egress route table for eu-north and enable more aggressive retries at the gateway. Applying now, will monitor.
Maya: Also please open ticket with provider NOC, attach mtr/traceroute/pcap, ask about recent infra changes or firewall rules blocking ICMP. CS — please send a template message to impacted customers explaining we're investigating network path issues and mitigating.
Oncall-Tim: MSS clamp rolled to all eu-north edge nodes (clamp=1400). Pushing retry bump on gateway to 3 -> 5 and lowering token refresh window tolerance to avoid spurious auth errors.
Sahil: Post-mitigation metrics: gateway 502 rate down from 11% -> 2% over 12 minutes; p95 latency down ~180ms -> 60ms. Packet retransmits reduced dramatically.
Leah: Provider NOC ticket created (ref: NOC-5543). They acknowledged seeing drops and said they're investigating an MTU-affecting config change on their transit.
Maya: CS, please add this text to the customer update: "Root cause suspected path MTU/fragmentation issue with transit provider affecting eu-north egress; temporary TCP MSS clamp applied by Redwood; provider engaged."
cs-team: Will do, sending first update now.
Juan: Please keep the clamp in place until provider confirms fix. Also schedule a follow-up to remove it after we validate full path restores.
Oncall-Tim: Agreed. Keeping clamp and extra retries until provider closes ticket or we see stable telemetry for 2 hours.
Maya: Thanks all. Will capture timeline and assign postmortem owner once we hand off to infra. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Deploy log: route-change(eu-north) applied by Oncall-Tim at 7660012380.
Maya: Adding post-incident notes: impacted customers: ~18 (varied), main symptom: 502/gateway timeouts and auth refresh errors secondary.
Leah: Adding repro steps to incident doc: 1) run mtr to eg edge IP from remote vantage -> observe packet loss at provider hop; 2) run wget/curl larger payloads and see upstream reset if DF bit set; 3) tcpdump showing ICMP "frag needed" but no fragmented traffic.
Maya: Good. Closing slack thread for active ops — continuing in incident tracker.
